newsitem.title: GERMANY: BUBA'S ISSING - GERMANY SEEN FACING STABLE UPTURN.
newsitem.headline: BUBA'S ISSING - GERMANY SEEN FACING STABLE UPTURN.

text.p: Bundesbank directorate member Otmar Issing said on Thursday that most forecasts now envisaged Germany's economic upturn developing into a stable recovery, despite continued weak investment activity.

"In Germany there remains a clear trend towards recovery, even taking into account the catch-up effects which reinforced growth in the second quarter due to the weather-induced weakness at the start of the year," Issing said according to the text of a speech.
"It is especially supported by buoyant foreign demand," Issing said."
Even if investment remains weak, forecasts now dominate that the recovery could eventually develop into a stable upturn."
This hope was reflected in the latest economic forecasts, some of which had been heavily revised up, Issing said.
German gross domestic product (GDP) returned to strong growth of 1.5 percent in the second quarter of 1996.
The Bundesbank made the text available in Frankfurt before Issing, who is also the Bundesbank's chief economist, was due to give his speech at a monetary conference in Luxembourg.
